evidence: instruction.md reads as a first-person recruiting lead talking to a builder, with varied cadence and contractions, and no marketing gloss. Opening: 'Can you build HireOps, the workspace our recruiting team lives in all day? Two things happen in it.' (line 1, a terse fragment-like sentence after a question). Contractions and casual register: 'nobody's work gets trampled' (1), 'is ours to arrange' (3), 'layout and names are yours ... We don't need theme switching' (11), 'is your call ... so don't install packages. The server itself mustn't depend' (13). Concrete lived-in asides: 'I often move several candidates together' (3), 'without closing the card I have open, wiping the note I am typing or moving my cursor' (5), 'whether I am reading or halfway through a reply, never touch my draft' (7). Prose paragraphs, no bullet lists, no parallel-bullet structure. Grep for seamless|robust|delve|leverage|ensure|comprehensive|intuitive|streamline and em dashes returned no hit in instruction.md or hireops_rules.md. Even the runtime paragraph (13-15) stays in voice ('How you lay the other files and routes out under /app is your call', 'The browser side is free to pull fonts or a script from a CDN if that helps'). Notes voice: hireops_rules.md keeps the same team 'we/our' voice ('our recruiting workspace', line 3; 'what we care about is that the workspace behaves the way this note says', 4-5; 'Rejected off to the side', 43; 'Where drafts are kept is yours', 175). It is denser and uses bullets/tables, which is appropriate for a house rules document that the brief explicitly points to, and its bullets vary in length and form rather than being mechanically parallel. Minor observations (not defects for this row): (a) hireops_rules.md section 8 'Runtime file paths' (lines 196-202) and integration.md task-added lines 16-19 shift to a neutral system-documentation register ('The runtime may launch Node from a working directory other than the application directory'); integration.md lines 1-14 are template-controlled text, so this register is house convention for runtime notes, not LLM gloss. (b) Spelling register differs: instruction.md uses British 'honour' (line 13) while hireops_rules.md line 201 and integration.md line 8 use 'Honor'/'honoring'; this is a small cross-document inconsistency more relevant to row 3, and reads like two hands (a person plus a template) rather than robotic prose. (c) A few rules sentences are legalistic ('as soon as the workspace notices, at the latest on the next action that needs the server', 172-173), acceptable in a precise rules note. Counterexample search: tried to read the brief as an LLM-polished spec (uniform cadence, glossy adjectives, bulleted checklist); it does not fit, since sentence lengths range from 5 words to ~45 and the requests are framed as the speaker's own pain points. Broken-app / conforming-alternative probes are not applicable to this text-voice row; no runtime evidence is required, so the raw-evidence index was not needed for this verdict.
